hints: Look at all three statements as Group 2 trends going down from magnesium to calcium, think size, charge density and reactivity.
Remember that the smaller $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion polarises the carbonate ion more strongly, so $\text{MgCO}_3$ breaks up more easily on heating.
Check solubility of hydroxides and reducing power down the group, both increase from Mg to Ca, so see which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - thermal stability of carbonates**

Think polarising power. The smaller $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ distorts the large $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ion more than the larger $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ does.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Explain why MgCO3 decomposes easier**

Greater distortion weakens the C-O bond, so less heat is needed. That means $\text{MgCO}_3$ decomposes at a lower temperature than $\text{CaCO}_3$. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - solubility of hydroxides**

For Group 2, hydroxides become more soluble down the group. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is almost insoluble, while $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble.

Trend:
$$\text{solubility of M(OH)}_2 \text{ increases down group}$$

**Check statement 3 - reducing strength**

Reducing agent means electron donor. Reactivity increases down Group 2 because the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and lost more easily.

Trend:
$$\text{M} \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+} + 2e^-$$

**Conclude the combination**

Calcium loses electrons more readily than magnesium, so calcium is the stronger reducing agent. So statement 3 is correct. With 1, 2 and 3 all correct, choose the all-correct option.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. MgCO3 is less thermally stable, Ca(OH)2 is more soluble than Mg(OH)2, and Ca is more reactive and a stronger reducing agent than Mg.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. It correctly accepts the carbonate and hydroxide trends but wrongly rejects statement 3. Calcium is below magnesium, so it is more easily oxidised and is the stronger reducing agent.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. It misses statement 1. Students sometimes reverse the carbonate stability trend, but stability increases down the group, so MgCO3 definitely decomposes at a lower temperature.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. It misses statements 2 and 3. Both are standard down-group increases for Group 2, solubility of hydroxides and reducing power both increase from Mg to Ca.
